rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says the fire was in a thorn tree, though some People of the Book called it an acacia.
rows.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه، قال: خرج موسى نحوها، يعني نحو النار، فإذا هي في شجر من العليق، وبعض أهل الكتاب يقول في عوسجة

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: As Moses approached, the fire withdrew; when he turned back it came closer, and he felt afraid.
rows.anchor: فلما دنا استأخرت عنه، فلما رأى استئخارها رجع عنها، وأوجس في نفسه منها خيفة

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: The fire came near again; a voice from the tree reassured Moses, who then removed his sandals.
rows.anchor: فلما أراد الرجعة، دنت منه ثم كلم من الشجرة، فلما سمع الصوت استأنس

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One explanation is that the sandals were made from carrion donkey hide, which God did not want brought onto the sacred valley; Moses was to touch its blessing.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم: أمره بذلك، لأنهما كانتا من جلد حمار ميت، فكره أن يطأ بهما الوادي المقدس

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says the sandals were carrion donkey hide, and God wanted Moses to touch the sacred place.
rows.anchor: عن كعب، أنه رآهم يخلعون نعالهم {اخلع نعليك إنك بالواد المقدس طوى} فقال: كانت من جلد حمار ميت، فأراد الله أن يمسه القدس

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reports that Moses’ sandals were made of carrion donkey hide.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله {فاخلع نعليك} [طه: 12] قال: كانتا من جلد حمار ميت

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reports that the sandals were donkey hide and Moses removed them before approaching.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: حدثنا أن نعليه كانتا من جلد حمار، فخلعهما ثم أتاه

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali likewise says the sandals were donkey hide; the segment adds that Qatada held the same view.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب، {فاخلع نعليك} [طه: 12] قال: كانتا من جلد حمار، فقيل له اخلعهما قال: وقال قتادة مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view says the sandals were cowhide; God wanted Moses’ bare feet to receive the earth’s blessing.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: كانتا من جلد بقر، ولكن الله أراد أن يطأ موسى الأرض بقدميه، ليصل إليه بركتها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the sandals were cowhide and Moses was to touch the earth’s blessing directly; the valley had been sanctified twice.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: كانتا يعني نعلي موسى من بقر، ولكن إنما أراد الله أن يباشر بقدميه بركة الأرض، وكان قد قدس مرتين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid rejects the claim that the sandals were carrion hide: Moses was commanded to touch the earth’s blessing with his feet.
rows.anchor: وقيل لمجاهد: زعموا أن نعليه كانتا من جلد حمار أو ميتة، قال: لا، ولكنه أمر أن يباشر بقدميه بركة الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Najih glosses the command as bringing Moses’ feet into contact with the valley’s blessing.
rows.anchor: سمعت ابن أبي نجيح، يقول في قوله: {فاخلع نعليك إنك بالواد المقدس طوى} قال: يقول: أفض بقدميك إلى بركة الوادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that Moses remove the sandals to touch the blessed valley directly: the verse links the command to the valley’s sanctity, while neither the Qur’an nor an authoritative report establishes impurity or donkey hide.
rows.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: أمره الله تعالى ذكره بخلع نعليه ليباشر بقدميه بركة الوادي

rows.speaker: نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet describes Moses in wool garments and sandals of untanned donkey hide; al-Tabari says its chain needs scrutiny and would not rely on it without that problem.
rows.anchor: عن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال: " يوم كلم الله موسى، كانت عليه جبة صوف

rows.speaker: بعض قراء المدينة والبصرة
rows.claim: Some Medinan and Basran readers open the hamza of أني, making it a clause governed by نودي and meaning that this saying was called out.
rows.anchor: فقرأ ذلك بعض قراء المدينة والبصرة

rows.speaker: بعض عامة قراء المدينة والكوفة
rows.claim: Other leading Medinan and Kufan readers use kasra in إني, treating it as the start of a new clause: Moses was told, ‘I am your Lord.’
rows.anchor: وقرأه بعض عامة قراء المدينة والكوفة بالكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers kasra because يا موسى intervenes between نودي and إني; if the verb governed the clause, the construction would be نودي أن يا موسى إني.
rows.anchor: والكسر أولى القراءتين عندنا بالصواب، وذلك أن النداء قد حال بينه وبين العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari calls the valley purified and blessed; Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd also describe it as blessed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إنك بالواد المقدس} يقول: المبارك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the valley was sanctified and blessed twice.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد، قوله {إنك بالواد المقدس طوى} قال: قدس بورك مرتين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One interpretation takes طوى as a verbal noun meaning that Moses traversed the sacred valley.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم: معناه: إنك بالوادي المقدس طويته، فعلى هذا القول من قولهم طوى مصدر خرج من غير لفظه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses crossed the sacred land at night and went up to the valley’s higher part.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: قوله: {إنك بالواد المقدس طوى} يعني الأرض المقدسة، وذلك أنه مر بواديها ليلا فطواه

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes طوى to mean twice: God called Moses twice, in two calls.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: مرتين، وقال: ناداه ربه مرتين

rows.speaker: عدي بن زيد العبادي
rows.claim: Al-Tabari cites Adi ibn Zayd’s verse as evidence for طوى meaning repeated or twice.
rows.anchor: قول عدي بن زيد العبادي

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others transmit the poetic word as ثنى, meaning again and again, and say ثنى and طوى are synonymous.
rows.anchor: وروى ذلك آخرون: علي ثنى: أي مرة بعد أخرى، وقالوا: طوى وثنى بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the valley was sanctified twice and was named Ṭuwā.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {فاخلع نعليك إنك بالواد المقدس طوى} كنا نحدث أنه واد قدس مرتين، وأن اسمه طوى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the valley had been sanctified twice.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: كان قد قدس مرتين

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view treats Ṭuwā as the name of the valley.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل طوى: اسم الوادي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Ṭuwā is the name of the valley.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {طوى} [طه: 12] اسم للوادي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also identifies Ṭuwā as the valley’s name.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد: طوى: قال: اسم الوادي

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says Ṭuwā is the valley where Moses stood and received what God gave him, near the mountain.
rows.anchor: قال: قال ابن زيد، في قوله {بالواد المقدس طوى}

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another interpretation reads the phrase as God telling Moses to tread the valley barefoot.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل هو أمر من الله لموسى أن يطأ الوادي بقدميه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses طوى as an instruction to tread the valley.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قول الله تبارك وتعالى: {اخلع نعليك إنك بالواد المقدس طوى} قال: طأ الوادي

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima likewise interprets طوى as ‘tread the valley.’
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {طوى} [طه: 12] قال: طأ الوادي

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says Moses was to tread barefoot, as one enters the Kaaba barefoot, to receive the valley’s blessing.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، في قول الله {طوى} [طه: 12] قال: طأ الأرض حافيا، كما تدخل الكعبة حافيا، يقول: من بركة الوادي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses Ṭuwā as treading the earth barefoot.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، {طوى} [طه: 12] طأ الأرض حافيا

rows.speaker: بعض قراء المدينة
rows.claim: Some Medinan readers pronounce Ṭuwā with ḍamma and no tanwin, treating it as the name of the land; the uninflected place name Ḥunayn is their analogy.
rows.anchor: فلم يجر حنين، لأنه جعله اسما للبلدة لا للوادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading without tanwin also leaves Ḥirāʾ uninflected because it is treated as a place name, supporting the same analysis of Ṭuwā.
rows.anchor: ألسنا أكرم الثقلين رحلا … وأعظمهم ببطن حراء نارا فلم يجر حراء، وهو جبل، لأنه جعله اسما للبلدة

rows.speaker: عامة قراء أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: Most Kufan readers pronounce Ṭuwā with ḍamma and tanwin.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ذلك عامة قراء أهل الكوفة: {طوى} [طه: 12] بضم الطاء والتنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the reading with tanwin: it fits whether Ṭuwā is a verbal noun or, as he judges, a masculine valley name; as a name it is genitive in apposition to الوادي.
rows.anchor: وأولى القولين عندي بالصواب قراءة من قرأه بضم الطاء والتنوين، لأنه إن يكن اسما للوادي فحظه التنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Ṭuwā is the valley’s name, al-Tabari places it in the genitive as an appositive to الوادي.
rows.anchor: وهو عندي اسم الوادي. وإذ كان ذلك كذلك، فهو في موضع خفض ردا على الوادي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Tabari explains that Moses and Aaron were to speak gently to Pharaoh; al-Suddi says this means addressing him by his kunya.
rows.anchor: عن السدي: {فقولا له قولا لينا} [طه: 44] قال: كنياه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes laʿalla here as a question: will Pharaoh reflect and return, or fear God and desist? Al-Tabari says this view has a sound basis.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {لعله يتذكر أو يخشى} [طه: 44] يقول: هل يتذكر أو يخشى

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view takes laʿalla as ‘so that’: Moses and Aaron should summon and admonish Pharaoh in order that he reflect or fear; al-Tabari accepts both interpretations as valid.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى لعل ههنا كي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Aaron fear Pharaoh will hurry to punish them if they summon him to the mission God commanded.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، {أن يفرط علينا} [طه: 45] قال: عقوبة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فرط can describe an act that gets ahead of someone; a فارط is one who goes ahead of a group to water or a stopping place, as the cited rajaz says the foreigner got ahead and hastened upon us.
rows.anchor: قد فرط العلج علينا وعجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari distinguishes ifrāṭ, excess and transgression, from tafrīṭ, delay or negligence.
rows.anchor: وأما الإفراط: فهو الإسراف والإشطاط والتعدي. يقال منه: أفرطت في قولك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the feared action as punishment from Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، {أن يفرط علينا} [طه: 45] قال: عقوبة منه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says they feared Pharaoh would hasten against them as soon as they conveyed God’s speech or command.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى} [طه: 45] قال: نخاف أن يعجل علينا إذ نبلغه كلامك أو أمرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Moses and Aaron not to fear Pharaoh because He is with them, helps them, hears their exchange, and gives them their answers.
rows.anchor: ما يجري بينكما وبينه، فأفهمكما ما تحاورانه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees what Moses, Aaron, and Pharaoh do; none of it is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: ما تفعلان ويفعل، لا يخفى علي من ذلك شيء

rows.speaker: حجاج
rows.claim: A report says God hears their conversation, reveals their response to them, and enables them to answer Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: قال: ثني حجاج {قال لا تخافا إنني معكما أسمع وأرى} [طه: 46] ما يحاوركما فأوحي إليكما فتجاوبانه

words: إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Aaron demand that Pharaoh release Israel and stop imposing degrading work; they offer a miracle to prove their mission if he doubts them, and declare safety for whoever follows God’s guidance.
rows.anchor: يقول: والسلامة لمن اتبع هدى الله، وهو بيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this expression, على and لِـ convey the same sense.
rows.anchor: يقال: السلام على من اتبع الهدى، ولمن اتبع بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs shown to Pharaoh were all the proofs and arguments establishing the truth of the mission entrusted to Moses and Aaron.
rows.anchor: أرينا فرعون آياتنا، يعني أدلتنا وحججنا على حقيقة ما أرسلنا به رسولينا، موسى وهارون إليه كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh denied and refused the truth brought by Moses and Aaron out of arrogance and obstinacy.
rows.anchor: أن يقبل من موسى وهارون ما جاءا به من عند ربهما من الحق استكبارا وعتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most Medinan and Basran readers and some Kufans read ساحر with alif, while most Kufans read سحر without it. Al-Tabari accepts both as close in meaning: the sorcerer plots through illusion and sorcery deceives by illusion.
rows.anchor: والقول في ذلك عندي أنهما قراءتان مشهورتان متقاربتا المعنى، وذلك أن الكيد هو المكر والخدعة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A reading with accusative كيد and uninflected سحر is attributed to some, but al-Tabari rejects it because the authoritative readers agree against it.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر عن بعضهم أنه قرأ: «كيد سحر» بنصب كيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says no sorcerer succeeds anywhere; some interpret this as killing the sorcerer wherever found. A Basran grammarian reports Ibn Masud’s أين أتى reading, while another grammarian treats examples like من حيث لا تعلم as queries asking where water and pasture are.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره من أهل العربية الأول: جزاء يقتل الساحر حيث أتى وأين أتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative omits an understood clause: Moses threw his staff, which swallowed what the magicians had made.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا الكلام متروك قد استغني بدلالة ما ترك عليه وهو: فألقى موسى عصاه، فتلقفت ما صنعوا

rows.speaker: سعيد
rows.claim: Saʿid reports that Moses’ staff became a huge serpent, swallowed all the magicians’ ropes and staffs, then returned to a staff; the magicians prostrated, while Pharaoh claimed Moses taught them and threatened crosswise amputation and crucifixion.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد، قال: لما اجتمعوا وألقوا ما في أيديهم من السحر خيل إليه من سحرهم أنها تسعى

rows.speaker: سعيد
rows.claim: In Saʿid’s account, Pharaoh was the first to cut off hands and feet crosswise and to crucify people on palm trunks.
rows.anchor: قال: فكان أول من قطع الأيدي والأرجل من خلاف فرعون {ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل} [طه: 71] قال: فكان أول من صلب في جذوع النخل فرعون

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the staff ate every snake the magicians made, after which they prostrated and professed faith in the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، {فأوجس في نفسه خيفة موسى}

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb reports that Moses feared the apparent moving serpents, but God reassured him; his staff swallowed every rope and staff before becoming a staff again, and the magicians believed it could not be sorcery since it defeated them.
rows.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه، {فأوجس في نفسه خيفة موسى}

words: ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ
rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says Pharaoh angrily saw he had been overcome when the magicians believed; al-Tabari explains his accusation as asking whether they had affirmed Moses before permission, and calls Moses their chief and greatest sorcerer who taught them.
rows.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه، قال: لما قالت السحرة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Tabari explains crosswise cutting as removing opposite hands and feet and says Pharaoh was the first to do it; al-Suddi reports that Pharaoh killed and cut the magicians after his threat.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، قال فرعون: {فلأقطعن أيديكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here في means ‘on’ the palm trunks; the condemned person was stretched along the tree, so Arabic describes him as crucified in it. The cited verse uses the phrase with a trunk as support.
rows.anchor: يقول: ولأصلبنكم على جذوع النخل، كما قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the magicians recognized the sign as from God and prostrated; Pharaoh then threatened them with crosswise amputation and crucifixion.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they began the day as magicians and ended it as martyrs after praying for patience and to die as Muslims.
rows.anchor: كما قال عبد الله بن عباس حين قالوا: {ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا وتوفنا مسلمين} [الأعراف: 126] وقال: كانوا في أول النهار سحرة، وفي آخر النهار شهداء

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says Aaron feared that if he went with the believers who followed him, others would remain behind, and Moses would accuse him of splitting Israel.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قول الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that Aaron feared the Israelites would divide into two groups and kill one another until they were destroyed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج، {إني خشيت أن تقول، فرقت بين بني إسرائيل ولم ترقب قولي} [طه: 94] قال: كنا نكون فرقتين فيقتل بعضنا بعضا حتى نتفانى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the explanation that Moses blamed Aaron for not following his command with the believers; Aaron feared Moses would say he had split the community by leaving some behind. Aaron’s appeal to the people and their refusal to leave the calf support this reading.
rows.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب، القول الذي قاله ابن عباس من أن موسى عذل أخاه هارون على تركه اتباع أمره بمن اتبعه من أهل الإيمان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says لم ترقب قولي means ‘you did not preserve my command’; al-Tabari glosses it as not attending to Moses’ words and preserving them, from the sense of مراقبة as observing and keeping in view.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {ولم ترقب قولي}
